- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive pessimism.  
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and continues upward; reduce forecast slope or add a ceiling to prevent overextension.  
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days, model may be overreacting to short-term sentiment; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen momentum.  
- When sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add a slight upward bias to counteract downward drift.  
- If model consistently forecasts higher than true outcome in early days of a 30-day window, it may be overestimating short-term volatility; reduce early forecast values by 1–2% relative to recent mean.  
- If sentiment is volatile and price moves sharply, model tends to overfit recent sentiment; use a 3–5 day smoothing filter to reduce noise-driven overreaction.
